The successful candidate will be responsible for preparing accurate and competitive cost estimates for civil construction projects from tender stage through to project award. - Strong understanding of civil construction methodologies, materials, plant and productivity rates.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications and tender documentation.
- Strong quantity take-off and cost-analysis skills.
- Experience obtaining and analysing subcontractor and supplier quotations.
- Good commercial awareness and understanding of construction contracts.
- Strong numerical, analytical and problem-solving abilities.
- High attention to detail and ability to work accurately under tender deadlines.
- Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills.
- Competency with estimating/take-off software.

This is an excellent opportunity for an engineering professional seeking exposure to both technical and asset management focused work within a large and complex transport environment.
About You

- A recognised Engineering Degree that satisfies the requirements for professional membership with Engineers Australia.
- Demonstrated experience in the planning, design, construction and maintenance of track infrastructure and associated civil assets.
- Sound knowledge of standards and practices relating to the construction and maintenance of rail track infrastructure.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and engineering judgement skills, with the ability to deliver practical solutions.

Moving millions of people requires the skill and commitment of a talented workforce, one that is fostered by a culture of inclusivity and benefits from its diversity. This is ultimately what ensures the PTA delivers on our purpose while upholding our values every step of the way.

The PTA is an equal opportunity employer and encourages people with disability, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and persons from culturally diverse backgrounds to apply.

Who we are
Legeneering is a leading, Perth-based one-stop provider of flexible solutions for the brownfield oil and gas industry. With a strong foundation in asset maintenance complemented by leading technology, we work closely with our clients to understand their requirements, identify the right solutions and execute projects in a cost-effective and safe manner, ensuring the highest levels of productivity.
The Opportunity
Legeneering is looking for a motivated, well-organised Project Coordinator to join our Oil & Gas projects team. The team delivers structural, piping and mechanical scopes on FPSOs, fixed platforms, marine assets and Onshore sites for Tier 1 operators.
This role covers the whole project lifecycle. It starts when an RFQ lands and runs through FEED, detailed design and engineering, fabrication and offshore execution, finishing with close-out and invoicing. You will drive the commercial, technical and logistical coordination that turns a client enquiry into a safely delivered, fully closed-out project.
You will report to the Project Manager and work day to day with our engineers, drafters, technical writers, welding coordinator, workshop, mobilisation and project controls teams. You will also deal directly with clients, vendors and Classification Societies.
Duties and Responsibilities
Tender, RFQ and Proposal
- Register and track incoming RFQs, and coordinate site data, drawings and technical queries with the client.
- Support preparation of quotes and proposals, including estimates, labour build-ups, vendor and workshop pricing, schedules, assumptions and exclusions.
- Track quotes through submission, clarification and award.
Design and Engineering
- Coordinate detailed design deliverables with internal and third-party engineers and drafters, including calculations, Piping and Structural design drawings, load-test procedures and design reports.
- Manage document control, transmittals and revision status through internal Technical Authority review and client / Classification Society review to approval.
- Track technical queries, deviations and client comments to closure, and confirm scope freeze before execution.
Procurement and Fabrication
- Manage the quote-to-purchase-order cycle for materials, fabrication, tooling, consumables and third-party services.
- Work with our Workshop team to deliver all aspects of the Fabrication cycle and documentation.
- Work with our Welding Coordinator to develop and gain sign-off of ITPs, weld procedures and welder qualifications. Compile Manufacturer's Data Records (MDRs) and close out hold and witness points.
- Arrange third-party inspection, load testing and T4 certification of tooling, lifting equipment and fabricated items.
Offshore Execution Readiness and Mobilisation
- Coordinate workpack development with the Technical Writer through review to Rev 0 sign-off.
- Review campaign requirements across equipment, tooling, consumables, labour and competencies, and close out any gaps, including training through Learning & Development.
- Confirm POB availability and execution dates with the client, submit mobilisation requests, and coordinate personnel, flights and freight with the Mobilisation team.
Execution, Close-out and Commercial
- Support the offshore campaign. Identify scope variations, prepare variation quotes and track variation POs so work continues without delay.
- Coordinate demobilisation, as-built documentation, completion records and job close-outs.
- Work with Project Controls to raise invoices and progress them through client sign-off and submission.
Project Controls and Reporting
- Keep the project tracker and records complete and current across all live jobs, from RFQ through to completion.
- Report schedule, cost, commercial and status information accurately to the Project Manager.
- Identify, manage and escalate risks, and contribute to lessons-learnt reviews.
- Promote safe work and QHSE compliance across all project phases.
Minimum Requirements
- Project Management, Engineering or Trade qualification.
- 3+ years' project coordination or project engineering experience in oil and gas, marine or mining, ideally in a contracting environment that covers design through to delivery.
- Working knowledge of engineering document control, procurement, fabrication QA (ITPs, MDRs) and offshore campaign preparation.
- Exposure to Classification Society (Lloyd's Register / ABS / DNV) requirements is highly regarded.
- Demonstrated ability to manage the commercial cycle on your own projects: quotes, POs, variations and invoicing.
- Strong organisation and communication skills. You must be able to run multiple concurrent jobs at different stages and coordinate across disciplines.
- Participation in company QHSE programs, active participation in cultural engagement, and completion of the cultural safety training package.
Highly Regarded
- Offshore experience or a current offshore medical, BOSIET/FOET and MSIC.
- Experience with ERP systems (M1 or similar) and strong Excel skills.
What We Offer
This is a permanent, Perth-based role in a close-knit projects team delivering work for Tier 1 operators. You will get end-to-end exposure across tender, engineering, fabrication and offshore delivery. The role has a defined career lattice from Project Coordinator through Senior Project Coordinator to Project Manager, with structured development against our Project Family Competency Matrix.
To apply, please submit your resume and a brief cover letter.

About Innovaero
Innovaero is an Australian aerospace engineering and drone manufacturing company delivering advanced unmanned systems for defence and commercial customers. The company designs, builds, and flight-tests sophisticated unmanned aerial platforms and is entering a strong growth phase as programs, teams, and international activity expand.
Role Description
Innovaero is seeking hands-on Manufacturing / Production Engineers to help establish and scale the manufacture of advanced autonomous aerial systems.
Working closely with our Product Engineering, Production and Quality teams, you will help design and implement the manufacturing processes, equipment, tooling and production systems required to transition complex products from engineering development into repeatable serial manufacture.
The role will initially support the establishment of a new manufacturing facility and production capability for products incorporating mechanical, composite, electronic, propulsion and software-integrated systems.
 Key Responsibilities
- Develop manufacturing processes and production methods for new and existing products.
- Design production layouts, workstations, tooling, jigs, fixtures and test equipment.
- Specify, evaluate, procure and commission manufacturing equipment.
- Support New Product Introduction (NPI), production ramp-up and transfer from engineering development into serial manufacture.
- Work with design engineers to improve products for manufacturability, assembly, testability and cost (DFM/DFA/DFT).
- Develop production routings, assembly sequences, labour standards and cycle-time estimates.
- Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation, work instructions, process specifications and production records.
- Support process qualification, validation and production-readiness activities.
- Establish appropriate process controls, traceability and manufacturing quality requirements.
- Undertake process capability studies, root-cause investigations and continuous-improvement activities.
- Support the introduction and effective use of ERP, MES and digital manufacturing systems.
- Work directly with production personnel to resolve manufacturing issues and progressively improve safety, quality, cost and throughput.
Note training will be provided on equipment where required.
Qualifications & Skills:
- Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Mechatronics, Aerospace or a related engineering discipline.
- 3+ years’ manufacturing engineering or industrialisation experience with complex engineered products; experience in scaled or serial production is preferred.
- Demonstrated experience turning engineering designs into practical, repeatable manufacturing processes.
- Strong practical engineering capability and a willingness to work directly on the production floor.
Experience in one or more of the following would be advantageous:
- Aerospace, defence, automotive, electronics or other complex product manufacturing.
- Composite manufacturing.
- Electronics integration and electromechanical assembly.
- New Product Introduction and production ramp-up.
- Production-line design, automation, tooling or industrial engineering.
- ERP and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES).
- AS9100 or similar regulated manufacturing environments.
Applicants must have full, permanent work rights in Australia. Applicants must be able to obtain National Police and other related security clearances that apply to the role.
How to Apply:
If you meet the above requirements and would like to be considered for this role, please click on the apply button and follow the prompts. We will get in touch if you are shortlisted for this opportunity.

candidates.title: Medium Term Mine Planning Engineer

candidates.content_text:
The CSA Mine is located 11 kilometres north-west of Cobar, central western New South Wales. At 1.9 kilometres deep, it is one of Australia’s deepest underground mines and is Australia’s highest-grade copper mine.
Harmony is the largest gold producer by volume in South Africa and is a significant operator of gold tailings retreatment facilities. CSA Mine has recently joined Harmony Australasia, marking the beginning of an exciting new chapter. The acquisition underpins Harmony’s strategy to expand its Australasian footprint and establish a strong, diversified copper portfolio, complemented by the Eva Copper Mine Project in Queensland, currently under construction, and set to become the state’s largest open‑pit copper mine upon commissioning. In Papua New Guinea, Harmony owns and operates the Hidden Valley mine and owns 50% of the Tier 1 Wafi-Golpu copper-gold project. These assets are supported by the Harmony Australasia regional corporate office located in Milton, Brisbane.
Reporting to the Senior Strategic Planning Engineer, the Medium-Term Mine Planning Engineer plays a critical role in driving and influencing the mine plan to achieve the operations medium to long term targets. You will play an integral part in ensuring the medium-long range forecasts are effectively derisked and stabilised resulting in improved production and safety.
Roster:
This role will be based onsite in Cobar, NSW working an 8/6 days FIFO roster from Brisbane or Sydney with local candidates highly regarded.
Key Responsibilities:
- Manage and produce the 3 monthly rolling schedules & 12-month forecasts in line with the annual budget requirements and escalate appropriately where risks to the plan arise.
- Effectively communicate the 3MRS & 12-month rolling forecasts to key site stakeholders and leadership team on a fortnightly basis
- Work within a 3–36-month timeframe to develop considered, optimised and practical medium-term designs for development (Operational and Capital) and stopes.
- Provide guidance to the short-term scheduling team where required, to ensure that the weekly plan is aligned to the 3MRS and moreover, the yearly budget.
- Liaise with required stakeholders to deliver achievable and practical plans & designs.
About You:
To be successful, you will bring the following skills, experience and personal attributes:
- Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering or related field.
- 5+ years’ underground hard rock experience in mine design/planning and scheduling essential (Experience in ventilation well regarded)
- Demonstrated ability to work in a team environment and communicate effectively with operational and contractor teams.
- Experience using mine planning software - Deswik, Sched & CAD.
- Flexible and capable of adapting to a dynamic work environment.
Benefits:
- Competitive salary including eligibility to participate in bonus scheme.
- Opportunity to grow your career within a dynamic international organisation.
- Health and wellbeing initiatives, including access to gym and pool facilities to our employees and their dependants in Cobar.
- Join a business that is growing in Australia and exposed to the high growth commodities of copper and gold.
To Apply:
If you believe you have the skills, knowledge and experience to fulfil this role, please submit your application online by clicking ‘Apply’. Please include a Cover Letter which outlines how your skills and experience align with this role.
We thank all applicants for your interest and the time taken to submit your application. While we consider all suitable applicants, only those short-listed for interview will be contacted.
Please note: All candidates must have the right to live and work in Australia and will be required to undertake a comprehensive pre-employment medical screen, including drug and alcohol testing.
To learn more about Harmony and CSA Mine, please visit: https://www.harmony.co.za/operations/australia/csa-copper-mine/

The Design & Placemaking Services Branch plays a key role in planning and delivering infrastructure solutions that support one of Australia’s fastest-growing regions. You hold tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering or a related discipline and have experience delivering engineering, infrastructure or project-based outcomes within a complex environment.
You thrive on managing projects.

You are a skilled communicator.
You build productive relationships with stakeholders at all levels and have proven skills in consultation, negotiation, problem solving and achieving positive outcomes.

Once you have these two documents ready, click ‘Apply Now’ and follow the prompts to complete your application.
